title: [Awake] Longer tray intervals and Settings editor for tray time shortcuts

proposed_comments.title: Preserve saved tray shortcuts when labels collide
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve saved tray shortcuts when labels collide

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `CanAddTrayTime` and `SaveTrayTimes` in `src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/ViewModels/AwakeViewModel.cs`.

**Problem:** Addition checks duplicate seconds but not the dictionary key generated from the duration. An existing custom key can equal the new duration's formatted label while storing a different duration. If the existing duration sorts first, addition reports success but silently drops the new shortcut; otherwise it silently replaces the existing duration. `TryAdd` ignores the duplicate after the persisted dictionary has already been cleared.

**Why it matters:** Existing custom labels are supported configuration, so a valid legacy label can cause a successful-looking edit to lose saved data.

**Suggested change:** Check both duration uniqueness and ordinal equality with the generated label in `CanAddTrayTime`. In `SaveTrayTimes`, construct and validate the complete duration-ordered dictionary before changing persisted settings, then clear and explicitly add its entries to the existing dictionary. Preserve historical labels and the init-only `CustomTrayTimes` dictionary identity; do not assign a replacement dictionary or silently ignore duplicate keys.

**Verification:** Using the existing deterministic test formatter, which labels 3600 seconds as `3600s`, cover that custom key storing either 600 or 7200 seconds. Assert that addition is rejected and the existing value/count remain unchanged. Both cases fail on the original implementation and pass with this correction; the label is a unit-test fixture, not a claim about the localized UI text. The affected Settings build and all 14 Awake tests pass with the coordinated correction; live tray/IPC interaction has not been exercised.

confidence.rationale: Two real original-source Settings regressions fail and pass with the localized correction; dictionary identity is retained.

proposed_comments.title: Disable deletion of the final tray shortcut
proposed_comments.body:
### Disable deletion when only one tray shortcut remains

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** The `AwakeTrayTimeItem` template in `AwakePage.xaml`, `AwakeTrayTimeItem.cs`, and `AwakeViewModel.RefreshTrayTimes`.

**Problem:** The delete button has no enabled-state binding, while `RemoveTrayTime` rejects removal of the last item. Users can still activate a button that then does nothing.

**Why it matters:** The visible and accessibility-enabled action should agree with the last-shortcut safeguard.

**Suggested change:** Add a read-only `CanRemove` value to each tray item, preserving the existing two-argument constructor compatibility. Set it from the complete refreshed item count when rebuilding `TrayTimes`, and bind the template button's `IsEnabled` to `CanRemove` with `Mode=OneTime`. Each refresh recreates the immutable items, so their bound state is refreshed after deletion, addition and reset. Do not bind `ViewModel.CanRemoveTrayTime` directly inside this template: its compiled data type is `AwakeTrayTimeItem`, not the page.

**Verification:** Cover two-to-one, one-to-two and reset transitions, including the single-item removal rejection. The actual Settings XAML build and all 14 affected Awake tests pass with the coordinated item/refresh/template correction. Interactive keyboard, screen-reader and tray behavior have not been exercised.

confidence.rationale: Original button is unbound while removal is guarded; compiled typed-template correction and all count transitions pass. No interactive UI claim.
